BiblicalUsage: Na'em means to be agreeable or pleasant, and it holds some of the tenderest words in Scripture. In 2 Samuel 1:26 David says of Jonathan, very pleasant hast thou been unto me, and in Ezekiel 32:19 the question is asked, whom dost thou pass in beauty, in a taunt over the fallen.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that pleasantness is a gift when it is real, and a trap when it is only appearance; david's lament shows what true affection sounds like, and Ezekiel shows what happens when beauty is trusted instead of God.
